title: CANR Alumni Board highlights engagement and support for Michigan State University community
text:
The College of Agriculture and Natural Resources (CANR) at Michigan State University highlighted on Apr. 15 the role of its Alumni Board in connecting nearly 60,000 alumni worldwide with opportunities to engage with the college after graduation.
The CANR Alumni Board aims to strengthen relationships among alumni, students, faculty, and friends of MSU. Volunteer members represent each department within the college as well as MSU Extension, young alumni, and at-large members. These volunteers meet quarterly in East Lansing to coordinate activities such as promoting college events, supporting fundraising efforts like Give Green Day, awarding student club grants and scholarships, and selecting recipients for annual awards.
Nicole Sevrey serves on the CANR Alumni Executive Board as an at-large member representing Michigan Farm Bureau. She said her experience at CANR provided a strong foundation for her career: “CANR gave me a practical foundation for the work I do today. It wasn’t just what I learned in the classroom, but also the exposure to real issues in agriculture and the people behind them that stuck with me. That experience shaped how I approach communications now, especially when it comes to policy and advocacy.” Sevrey encouraged current students by saying: “Don’t underestimate the value of relationships and experiences—this industry is built on them… strong writing skills will set you apart… The skills you’re building are incredibly transferable, especially in communications and leadership.” She added that staying engaged helps maintain a sense of community: “Staying engaged in small ways can make a big difference… CANR is a special place, and staying involved helps keep that sense of community strong.”
The College addresses challenges related to food systems, health outcomes, and environmental sustainability through education programs and outreach initiatives according to its official website . The institution reported an enrollment of 3,735 students during fall 2021 while engaging more than 340 scientists across various research areas according to its official website . To extend its impact throughout Michigan communities beyond campus boundaries, CANR collaborates through 15 major research centers as well as MSU Extension services according to its official website .
As part of ongoing efforts to foster connections within its network—including current students—the college has begun releasing spotlights on individual board members sharing their motivations for service.
Sevrey concluded by describing her hopes for her tenure: “I’d really like to help strengthen the connection between students and the real-world opportunities waiting for them. I’d also love to help bolster the support for CANR student clubs and the invaluable experiences they provide.”
summary: Nicole Sevrey serves on the CANR Alumni Executive Board as an at-large member representing Michigan Farm Bureau.
